references.text: The original regulation concerning the daily burnt offering with two one-year-old lambs, one in the morning and one in the evening, given at Sinai.
The requirement that sacrificial animals must be without blemish (תָמִים) to be acceptable to the Lord.
Rules for the burnt offering (עֹלָה) and how it is to be kept burning continuously on the altar.
Ezekiel's vision of the restored temple includes the daily burnt offering with a one-year-old lamb each morning.
The prophecy that the daily offering (תָּמִיד) will be removed, implying its continuous practice.
Reference to the abolition of the daily offering as a sign of desecration.
The daily sacrifices, which were repeated continuously, could never make the worshippers perfect and point forward to Christ's final sacrifice.
John the Baptist identifies Jesus as "the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world," fulfilling the role of the sacrificial lamb.
Christ is described as a lamb without blemish or spot, fulfilling the requirement of תְמִימִם (without blemish) in the law of offerings.
